title: Condicional hipotético: si + pretérito imperfecto de subjuntivo

sections.content: To ask "what if" about a past that didn't happen, pair si + past subjunctive (hubiera invertido) with the conditional perfect (habría sido) -- exactly the tool a counterfactual history argument needs. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Si esos ingresos se hubieran invertido de manera sistemática en infraestructura, la historia económica del país habría sido muy distinta.
items.english: If that revenue had been invested systematically in infrastructure, the country's economic history would have been very different.

items.spanish: Si el Perú hubiera diversificado su economía durante estas décadas, habría estado mucho mejor preparado para lo que vino después.
items.english: If Peru had diversified its economy during these decades, it would have been much better prepared for what came next.

items.spanish: Si esos sustitutos hubieran tardado unas décadas más en desarrollarse, es posible que Perú hubiera tenido más tiempo para adaptarse.
items.english: If those substitutes had taken a few more decades to develop, Peru might have had more time to adapt.

items.spanish: Si cualquiera de estos países hubiera dependido de dos o tres exportaciones, probablemente habría amortiguado mejor cada una de estas crisis.
items.english: If any of these countries had depended on two or three exports, it would probably have cushioned each of these crises better.

sections.content: Both halves look back at an unreal past: si + hubiera + participle for the condition, habría + participle for the result -- never si + habría, which is a common learner error.
